fixes.explanation: Counted? Friend, I count cookies by the dozen all day, and even I wouldn't have lined anybody up for a headcount right then. The verse says that after the whole nation had been circumcised, they stayed there in the camp until they were healed (Joshua 5:8). I bet nobody was in a hurry to go anywhere.

Bethel is like grabbing the crushed peppermint when the recipe says chocolate chips. Good topping, different batch. The LORD says to Joshua, “Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you.” Then the verse says, “So that place has been called Gilgal to this day.” (Joshua 5:9).

Shiloh is a fine name, baker, but this batch is labeled Gilgal. After the LORD rolls away the reproach of Egypt, the text says, “So that place has been called Gilgal to this day.” (Joshua 5:9). It's the same Gilgal where Israel is camped when they keep the Passover (Joshua 5:10).

Sabbath, I see you, friend. After all that healing, I bet everybody wanted a day off. But Joshua 5:10 says that on the evening of the fourteenth day, they kept the Passover. The Sabbath never shows up in this passage.

Purim is a deep cut, baker, and I respect the reach! But Joshua 5:10 says that on the evening of the fourteenth day, camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho, the Israelites kept the Passover. Purim isn't in this passage. It's a holiday guest who showed up at the wrong party.

The cloud isn't in this passage, friend. What ceased was the manna. “There was no more manna for the Israelites, so that year they began to eat the crops of the land of Canaan.” (Joshua 5:12). One day it's manna, the NEXT day it's crops! I bet that was a big morning.
